rules: When the effective privilege mode is S-mode or U-mode, the satp CSR is considered active.
Executions of the address-translation algorithm may only begin using a given value of satp when satp is active.
If SXLEN=32 and software writes zero to bits 30-0 of satp, the MODE is set to Bare.
If SXLEN=64 and software writes zero to bits 59-0 of satp, the MODE is set to Bare.
When satp.MODE is Bare, supervisor virtual addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses.
When satp.MODE is Bare, there is no additional memory protection beyond the physical memory protection scheme.

If satp is written with a value where satp.MODE is Bare but the remaining fields (bits 30-0 for SXLEN=32 or bits 59-0 for SXLEN=64) are nonzero, the effect on the value of the remaining fields and on address translation and protection behavior is unspecified.
If satp is written with an unsupported MODE, the entire write has no effect and no fields in satp are modified.
The implemented ASID bits (ASIDLEN) are determined by writing one to every bit position in the ASID field and reading back the value in satp to see which bit positions hold a one.
If ASIDLEN > 0, the bits satp.ASID[ASIDLEN-1:0] are writable.
When SXLEN=32 and satp.MODE is Sv32, supervisor virtual addresses are translated into supervisor physical addresses via a two-level page table.
When SXLEN=64 and satp.MODE is Sv39, supervisor virtual addresses are translated into supervisor physical addresses via a three-level page table.
When SXLEN=64 and satp.MODE is Sv48, supervisor virtual addresses are translated into supervisor physical addresses via a four-level page table.
When SXLEN=64 and satp.MODE is Sv57, supervisor virtual addresses are translated into supervisor physical addresses via a five-level page table.
During the address-translation process, the root page table base address is determined by satp.PPN multiplied by PAGESIZE.
Implementations must only perform implicit reads of the translation data structures pointed to by the current contents of the satp register or a subsequent valid translation data structure entry.
Changing satp.MODE from Bare to other modes and vice versa takes effect immediately without the need to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
Changes to satp.ASID take effect immediately without the need to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
If satp.MODE is read-only zero, the implementation may make senvcfg.FIOM read-only zero.
If satp.MODE is read-only zero, attempts to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction might raise an illegal-instruction exception.
